I am 52 years old and have farmed these 18.4 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. I finished high school, so I don't just copy neighbors blindly. I keep records of input costs and yields in a notebook, and I talk to the seed dealer in the township and check prices on my phone before I decide. My soil is light loam with decent base fertility, but after six years of cotton on one block, I know the potassium is getting drawn down.

My land is split into two blocks. The 10 mu on the east side does wheat-maize double cropping every year. The other 8.4 mu is my cotton land.

For the winter wheat, it is already in the ground from last October. I used an improved semi-dwarf variety. Right now it is greening up. Last year I applied 20 kg of nitrogen per mu, but the yield only reached 480 kg because the grain filling was weak. This year I will push nitrogen to 24 kg per mu, applying it in three splits: 10 kg at green-up, 8 kg at jointing, and 6 kg at heading. Phosphorus stays at 9 kg per mu as base fertilizer, potassium at 7 kg. My soil drains well, so I need four irrigations in total: winter irrigation is already done, plus jointing water, heading water, and grain-filling water from my well. I budget two pesticide sprays for wheat—one herbicide and one fungicide-insecticide mix. Expected yield should reach 520 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For summer maize on the same 10 mu, I will plant a hybrid variety right after wheat harvest in early June. Maize responds well to fertilizer. I will apply 20 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I use rotary tillage immediately after wheat harvest to chop the straw and prepare the seedbed. Two irrigations are enough for maize here—one at the big trumpet stage and one at filling. Two pesticide applications: one at seedling stage and one during ear development. I expect 580 kg per mu.

For cotton on the 8.4 mu, I use an improved Bt cotton variety. Cotton needs careful nutrient balance or it grows too many leaves and drops bolls. I learned this the hard way over 20 years of growing it. I will apply 19 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. Potassium is important because cotton is a heavy K feeder. I will rotary till the land in late April before planting. Four irrigations: planting water, flowering water, boll-setting water, and boll-opening water. Cotton pests are serious here, so I budget 5 pesticide sprays—mainly for bollworm, aphid, and red spider mite. Expected seed cotton yield is 300 kg per mu.

Fertilizer prices went up again this year. I calculated that total fertilizer cost will be about 8,500 yuan for all crops. It hurts, but last year my neighbor Chen cut nitrogen by 3 kg per mu on his wheat and lost almost 80 kg in yield. That is a false economy. With my son working in Shijiazhuang and sending money home, I can afford to invest properly. A bad harvest means I lose everything; wasting half a bag of fertilizer is just a cost I can absorb.
